  file-watch mechanisms can efficiently seek straight to the end of the file and process
  newly arrived bytes immediately. Whole-file replacements frequently involve atomic
  renames or inode changes, which complicate tracking and risk breaking active file
  descriptors for readers. Ultimately, append-only designs drastically reduce I/O overhead
  and synchronization complexity for real-time monitoring and log aggregation.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> Without using any tools, write thirty short numbered sentences about terminal
  multiplexers. One sentence per line, numbered 1 to 30.

▸ Thought for 4s
  Begin Considering Parameters

  1. A terminal multiplexer allows multiple terminal sessions to be managed within a
  single window.
  2. Popular terminal multiplexers include tmux, GNU Screen, and Zellij.
  3. They enable running multiple command-line programs simultaneously without opening
  separate GUI windows.
  4. Multiplexers operate using a client-server architecture to persist background
  sessions.
  5. A major benefit is the ability to detach from an active session and reattach to it
  later.
  6. Detached sessions continue executing processes even if a user loses an SSH connection.
  7. Users can divide a single screen into multiple rectangular panes horizontally or
  vertically.
  8. Panes can be resized, swapped, zoomed, or closed independently.
  9. Multiplexers organize workflows into multiple distinct named windows or tabs within a
  session.
  10. Navigation between panes and windows is typically handled through configurable
  keyboard shortcuts.
  11. Most multiplexers use a customizable prefix key sequence to intercept user commands.
  12. Scrollback buffers allow users to navigate and search through historical terminal
  output.
  13. Built-in copy modes let users select and copy text directly without touch
⡿  Begin Considering Parameters...
